note: The register of what has been disqualified.
A retraction is not a deletion. The contract keeps every element it has
ever published — the identifier, the meaning, the value — because a
correction that erases the thing it corrects cannot be read afterwards.
What a retraction does is mark the element: it is not live, it was
carried in a named version, it was retracted on a named day, and the
reason is written down in one place.
The owner reserves the right to retract retroactively. This register is
how that right is exercised without rewriting the history: the element
stays where it is, marked; the projections carry the mark; and the gate
checks that the mark travelled, that nothing retracted is presented as
live, and that every mark has a reason.
A retraction is a fact about the system, like a deviation: it is not a
task, and it is not closed by a fix. It is superseded by a version that
carries the correction, and the mark says which.
